name: Logitech TrueForce Linux driver
description: Linux kernel driver and userspace tools for Logitech's direct-drive wheels (RS50, G PRO) and the G923: force feedback, TrueForce haptics, rev lights and wheel settings, with launch tooling for Proton games.
implementation_languages: Rust, C, Slint, Shell, C++, Python, Makefile, Nix, Batchfile
description_good_justification: The README opens with what the software does and which wheels it drives: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to install, how to report problems (tools/setup.sh report) and how to contribute: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing
contribution_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing describes what contributions are wanted (code, hardware testing, USB captures), what an issue must contain, and how the project is checked without a wheel.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md: sign-off (DCO), tests with the change, coding standards, commit messages, dependency and binary rules, hardware safety.
floss_license_justification: GNU General Public License v2.0 only, the kernel's own license: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/COPYING
license_location_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/COPYING at the top level of the repository.
documentation_basics_justification: README sections Getting started, Install, Force feedback in games, Configuring the wheel and Troubleshooting (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#getting-started), plus the wiki.
documentation_interface_justification: The sysfs interface is documented in https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SYSFS_API.md, the launcher and its environment in https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/LAUNCH_OPTIONS.md, the wheel protocol in https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/PROTOCOL_SPECIFICATION.md.
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository, wiki and every download (GitHub releases, AUR, COPR, OBS) are served over HTTPS.
english_justification: All documentation, issues and commit messages are in English.
maintained_justification: Releases and commits every week; 0.41.0 shipped 2026-09-12 with fixes from that week's reports: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/releases
repo_track_justification: Git; every change is a commit with author, date and message.
repo_interim_justification: Every change is pushed to master as it is made; releases are tags on master, there is no separate private development line.
version_unique_justification: Every release is a tag vX.Y.Z and a GitHub release of the same name: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic versioning: major for sysfs API breaks, minor for new wheels or attributes, patch for fixes and docs, as stated at the top of CHANGELOG.md.
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md, one dated section per release, and the same text on each GitHub release: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been reported against this project so far. CHANGELOG.md is where every fix is described, and a security fix would be identified there and in the release with its identifier.
report_process_justification: Issues on GitHub, as the README asks: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/issues. tools/setup.sh report prints the environment block an issue needs.
report_responses_justification: Bug reports are answered, usually the same day, with a diagnosis or a request for a specific capture; see any recent issue at https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered and either scheduled or explained: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository (Security tab, Report a vulnerability), with an email address as the fallback.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within a few days. No vulnerability report has been received so far.
build_justification: The kernel module builds with make (or DKMS), the userspace with cargo build; tools/setup.sh does the whole install from a checkout.
build_common_tools_justification: make and Kbuild for the kernel module, cargo for the Rust workspace, DKMS, and the distribution packagers' own tools (makepkg, debhelper, rpmbuild).
build_floss_tools_justification: Only FLOSS tools are needed: GCC or Clang with the kernel's Kbuild, the Rust toolchain, GNU make. The project is packaged for Arch, Debian, Fedora, openSUSE and NixOS from those alone.
test_justification: cargo test --workspace in userspace/logi-wheel (over a thousand tests), plus header-only C harnesses for the force maths under tests/ (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/tests/README.md).
test_invocation_justification: cargo test --workspace in userspace/logi-wheel; make -C tests/effect-math run; make -C tests/texture-merge run: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: Coverage is not measured yet. The registry, the parsers, the launcher planning and the proxy logic are tested; the hardware-facing paths are not, as they need a wheel.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/actions on every push and pull request.
test_policy_justification: Stated in the README's Contributing section: changes that add functionality come with tests for it, and CI runs them on every push (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing).
tests_are_added_justification: Recent commits show it: the marker sanitiser fix added a bash-backed test, the build stamp added unit and integration tests, the installer change added a packaging test (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/commits/master).
warnings_justification: The kernel module builds under the kernel's -Wall defaults on 5.15, 6.8 and 7.x in CI, with sparse and smatch on top; the Rust workspace builds with clippy -D warnings on every push.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any clippy warning in the Rust workspace, and the kernel module builds warning-free on every kernel CI builds against.
warnings_strict_justification: clippy with all warnings as errors on the Rust workspace; sparse with endian checking and smatch on the kernel module; checkpatch on style.
know_secure_design_justification: The driver's inputs are an untrusted USB device and untrusted game or Wine processes. The design keeps them apart: every parser is bounds-checked and fuzzed, device access goes through udev-granted permissions rather than root helpers, workflow tokens are read-only by default, releases are signed, and kernel-side lifetimes are reasoned about explicitly (see the 0.41.0 changelog entries on the deferred force-feedback teardown).
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer works on kernel memory-lifetime bugs (use-after-free in deferred callbacks, re-entrancy, lock ordering) and on input validation for network-fed parsers, documented in CHANGELOG.md and docs/; CodeQL's security queries run on the C.
crypto_published_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_call_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_floss_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_keylength_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_working_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography and opens no network connections beyond loopback UDP for game telemetry; release signing is GnuPG in the packaging pipeline.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_random_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
delivery_mitm_justification: Every download is HTTPS: GitHub releases and repository, AUR, COPR, OBS. The Arch repository and its packages are GPG-signed and pacman verifies them.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Release packages are signed and the signatures are attached to the release; the Arch repository database is signed; the Debian and RPM channels carry their own signing.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known vulnerability is outstanding; cargo-audit runs in CI and Dependabot watches dependencies.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: None reported so far; the policy in SECURITY.md is a fix on master and a release.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no keys or tokens; the signing key and channel credentials live in GitHub Actions secrets.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (C/C++, security queries) on every push and weekly; clippy with warnings as errors on the Rust workspace; sparse and smatch on the kernel module; SonarCloud: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/actions
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-and-quality query suite on the C, on every push and weekly; cargo audit for known-vulnerable dependencies.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open findings: clippy and cargo-audit gate every push, CodeQL alerts are triaged as they appear.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every push and pull request, plus a weekly CodeQL schedule.
dynamic_analysis_justification: cargo-fuzz targets for every parser fed from outside, and a debug kernel for the module.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The kernel module is exercised under a KASAN, lockdep and kmemleak debug kernel in the development VM for lifetime and locking changes; the Rust parsers are fuzzed with cargo-fuzz.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Fuzz targets run debug builds with Rust assertions enabled; the kernel module keeps WARN_ON checks in production builds.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis finding is open; the first fuzz run found nothing, and a panic found that way would be fixed before the next release.
dco_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md requires a Signed-off-by line under the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 on every commit.
access_continuity_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md, section Continuity: everything but the credentials is in the public repository; a successor generates and publishes their own signing key; the ninety-day rule is written down.
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer. GOVERNANCE.md says how a co-maintainer is made and why one is wanted; until then this is honestly unmet.
documentation_architecture_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/wiki/Architecture: components, interfaces at a glance, and where protocol knowledge lives; the module-level design of each part is in the crate and file headers.
documentation_security_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md: what runs where, the attack surface and threat model, the design principles, and what the software does not protect against.
documentation_quick_start_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#getting-started: install, plug in, one launch option; and the wiki's Installation page.
documentation_current_justification: Every release updates README, CHANGELOG, docs/STATUS.md and the wiki with it; the generated game table is a test that fails when the docs drift from the registry (tests/game_setup_doc.rs).
documentation_achievements_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#readme carries the CI, Scorecard and Best Practices badges, and docs/STATUS.md states what is verified and what is not.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The user-facing surfaces are a terminal app and a small settings window; the maintainer is red-green colorblind and the LED and status displays are designed on count and position rather than hue, but no accessibility standard is claimed.
internationalization_justification: The software has no user-facing text beyond diagnostics and the settings labels, and no localization; English only, stated in the documentation.
sites_password_security_justification: No project site stores passwords; GitHub does.
maintenance_or_update_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md, Supported versions: only the latest release is supported, stated for users and packagers.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md: reporters are credited in the advisory, the changelog and CREDITS.md unless they ask not to be.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md, What happens next: acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment within 14, fix and release within 60, coordinated publication with advisory and CVE.
coding_standards_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md: Linux kernel coding style for the driver, clippy with warnings as errors for the Rust workspace.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: CI runs checkpatch.pl over the kernel driver and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings over the Rust workspace on every push and pull request.
build_standard_variables_justification: The kernel module honours KDIR and the kernel's own build variables (CC, KCFLAGS); the Rust workspace uses cargo's standard ones (CARGO_TARGET_DIR, RUSTFLAGS).
build_preserve_debug_justification: Release builds use cargo's default release profile, which carries no debug information; the packages ship what cargo produces. Adding debug = 1 to the release profile is a one-line change not yet made.
build_non_recursive_justification: The Rust workspace is one cargo invocation; the kernel module is one Kbuild invocation; tests/ harnesses are single Makefiles.
build_repeatable_justification: Builds are from a locked dependency graph (Cargo.lock, --locked in CI and packages) and pinned toolchains; the same tag produces the same result on every channel, verified by the distribution builders.
installation_common_justification: Packages for Arch (AUR and a signed repository), Debian and Ubuntu, Fedora (COPR), openSUSE (OBS) and NixOS; tools/setup.sh for a checkout.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is by distribution package, each of which follows its own conventions; the from-source path is a convenience script that installs to the packages' locations. DESTDIR/PREFIX are not offered because the module goes through DKMS and the apps to the package paths the launcher expects.
installation_development_quick_justifica: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/wiki/Building-and-Contributing: cargo build in the workspace, make in mainline/, and sudo ./tools/setup.sh does the whole install.
external_dependencies_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/userspace/logi-wheel/Cargo.lock lists every Rust dependency with its version and checksum; the kernel module depends only on the kernel; GitHub Actions are pinned by hash in .github/workflows.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot (cargo and Actions, weekly) and cargo audit on every push and weekly; policy in docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Every dependency is a cargo crate updated through Cargo.lock; nothing is vendored or copied into the tree.
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are kept current by Dependabot; the kernel interface is tracked per kernel version with compatibility shims in the module (LINUX_VERSION_CODE checks) and CI builds on several kernels.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: CI runs the full Rust suite, the C harnesses, kernel builds on 5.15, 6.8 and current kernels, sparse, smatch and the Nix flake on every push and pull request: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/actions
regression_tests_added50_justification: Each bug fix in the recent releases carried a test that reproduces it (see the 0.40.x and 0.41.0 changelog entries and their commits): the marker sanitiser, the direction projection, the prefix lookup, the build stamp, the packaging tests.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured with cargo-llvm-cov over the whole Rust workspace on 2026-09-13: 80.2% region coverage, 80.0% line coverage, 83.3% of functions; per crate the core is at 91%, the relay 93%, the daemon 83%, the terminal app 81%, the proxy 68% and the GUI 57%. A CI job (Coverage) now measures it on every push and publishes the summary.
test_policy_mandated_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md: a change that adds functionality carries the tests for it; a bug fix carries a test that would have caught the bug.
implement_secure_design_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, Secure design principles: least privilege, validation at every boundary, fail closed on force, one writer per stream, nothing hidden in the build.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography and opens no network connections beyond loopback UDP for game telemetry; release signing is GnuPG in the packaging pipeline.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography and opens no network connections beyond loopback UDP for game telemetry; release signing is GnuPG in the packaging pipeline.
crypto_used_network_justification: No network communication beyond loopback UDP between local processes; nothing crosses a network.
crypto_tls12_justification: No TLS is used; the software makes no network connections beyond loopback.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The software implements and uses no cryptography and opens no network connections beyond loopback UDP for game telemetry; release signing is GnuPG in the packaging pipeline.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The software implements and uses no cryptography and opens no network connections beyond loopback UDP for game telemetry; release signing is GnuPG in the packaging pipeline.
signed_releases_justification: Every release asset is signed with the project's GnuPG key and the signature attached; the Arch repository database is signed; the key fingerprint is in the README: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/releases
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not GPG-signed; the release assets are. Signing tags needs the maintainer's key on the machine that tags, which the release process does not yet do.
input_validation_justification: Every input from a device, a socket or a HID node passes a length- and structure-checking parser before any field is used; those parsers are fuzzed (userspace/logi-wheel/fuzz).
hardening_justification: See the Silver answer: read-only workflow tokens, hash-pinned actions, secret scanning with push protection, loopback-only sockets, fail-closed force paths.
achieve_silver_justification: Depends on the Silver criteria above.
contributors_unassociated_justification: The code is written by one person; the hardware testers credited in CREDITS.md are significant contributors to the project's knowledge but not to its code, and this criterion asks for code contributors.
copyright_per_file_justification: Source files carry an SPDX license identifier but not a per-file copyright statement; planned, mechanical, not yet done.
license_per_file_justification: Every source file (C, headers, Rust, C++, shell, Python; 176 files) starts with SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only, or the SPDX identifier of its own license where a file is imported; verified by a grep over git ls-files.
small_tasks_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md asks for small, single-purpose changes and names the ways a newcomer can help (hardware reports, captures, documentation); the issue tracker carries the open hardware questions.
require_2FA_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md: every account with write access must use two-factor authentication; GitHub also requires it of contributors.
secure_2FA_justification: GitHub's two-factor methods (authenticator apps and security keys) are what is available; SMS is not used.
code_review_standards_justification: There is one maintainer and no second reviewer, so no review standard beyond CONTRIBUTING.md's requirements applies today; GOVERNANCE.md says how that changes with a co-maintainer.
two_person_review_justification: The maintainer's changes have no second human reviewer. Stated in GOVERNANCE.md as the first thing a co-maintainer would change.
build_reproducible_justification: The Rust workspace builds from a locked dependency graph with pinned toolchains and no timestamps in the binaries except the build stamp, which is the git describe of the source; the distribution builders (OBS, COPR) rebuild the same tag independently and get working packages.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: 80% statement coverage measured; 90% is not reached (the GUI is at 57%).
test_branch_coverage80_justification: cargo-llvm-cov reports 80.2% region coverage across the workspace on 2026-09-13; regions are LLVM's branch-level unit.
hardened_site_justification: The project site is github.com, which sets the standard security headers; the project hosts no site of its own.
security_review_justification: No independent security review has been performed. The assurance case in docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md is the maintainer's own.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: GitHub requires two-factor authentication for accounts that contribute code, and GOVERNANCE.md requires it of every account with write access to this repository.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub assigns no permissions to a new collaborator until the maintainer sets them; the repository has no default write access.
osps_ac_03_01_justification: Branch protection on master requires a pull request for every change; direct commits are refused. Status checks must pass before merging.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: Branch protection on master refuses deletion and force pushes.
osps_br_01_01_justification: The only pipeline that takes an input is the release workflow's manual tag, which its first job validates against the vX.Y.Z form before anything runs (.github/workflows/publish-release.yml, job validate). Pull-request pipelines use no PR metadata in commands.
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests from forks run with a read-only token and no access to secrets (GitHub's default); every workflow starts with a read-only token and the release workflow's secrets are only exposed to jobs on the release tag.
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, wiki, releases, AUR, COPR, OBS (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/README.md, Install).
osps_br_03_02_justification: Distribution over HTTPS, with GnuPG-signed release assets and a signed Arch repository database; the deb and rpm channels carry their own signatures.
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled on the repository; workflow tokens are read-only by default; GOVERNANCE.md's secrets policy forbids secrets in the tree, and the tree is checked before releases.
osps_do_01_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#readme covers installation, launch options per game, configuring the wheel and troubleshooting; the wiki has a page per topic.
osps_do_02_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md, Report a problem, and the README's Contributing section.
osps_le_02_02_justification: Released assets are under the same GPL-2.0-only license; the three committed Windows helper binaries are built from source in this repository under it.
osps_le_03_02_justification: Every package ships the COPYING file; every release is built from the tagged source that contains it.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/userspace/logi-wheel/Cargo.lock (direct and transitive Rust dependencies with checksums); the kernel module has no dependencies beyond the kernel.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: Three generated Windows binaries are committed under tools/ (an escape proxy DLL, a range proxy DLL and the telemetry relay executable), because the packaging channels build offline and cannot cross-compile them today. Each is rebuilt only by its script from committed source and byte-verified against that source in CI (tools/check-committed-dlls.sh, tools/build-relay.sh --check). Moving them to build-time generation on every channel is on the roadmap.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binaries in the tree are the three above, each reproducible from committed source by a committed script and byte-verified in CI; they are reviewable through that source.
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Every workflow declares top-level permissions: contents: read; a job gets more only by declaring it.
osps_br_04_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md, one dated section per release, reproduced on the GitHub release.
osps_br_05_01_justification: cargo with a locked dependency graph for the Rust workspace; DKMS and the distributions' own package builders for the module and packages.
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every release asset is GnuPG-signed with a detached signature attached to the release; the Arch repository database is signed.
osps_do_07_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/wiki/Building-and-Contributing and the README's Install section: kernel headers, DKMS, the Rust toolchain and the fontconfig headers for the window.
osps_gv_01_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md, Roles and Secrets: one maintainer holds every sensitive resource, named.
osps_le_01_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md requires the Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off on every commit.
osps_qa_03_01_justification: Branch protection requires the CI status checks to pass before a pull request merges into master; the maintainer can bypass with an explicit admin merge, which is a deliberate act.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: Pull requests run the full CI, including the Rust test suite and the C harnesses, and must pass before merging.
osps_sa_01_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, What runs where, and the wiki's Architecture page: every component, its privilege, and what it talks to.
osps_sa_02_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SYSFS_API.md (the kernel interface), https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/LAUNCH_OPTIONS.md (the launcher, environment and daemon ports), https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SHARED_MEMORY_RELAY.md (the relay datagram), https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/PROTOCOL_SPECIFICATION.md (the wheel protocol).
osps_sa_03_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, Attack surface and threat model: the most likely and most consequential problems, per source, with what stands in the way of each.
osps_vm_01_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md, What happens next: acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment within 14, fix within 60, coordinated publication.
osps_vm_03_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md: GitHub private vulnerability reporting, enabled on the repository.
osps_vm_04_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md: advisories in the repository's Security tab, fixes named in CHANGELOG.md, non-affecting dependency advisories in security/openvex.json.
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Each release job that attaches assets declares contents: write and nothing else; the CodeQL job declares security-events: write; every other job runs on the read-only default (.github/workflows).
osps_br_01_04_justification: The only collaborator input a pipeline accepts is the release workflow's manual tag, validated against the vX.Y.Z form before use.
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every asset name carries the release version (for example logi-wheel-0.41.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst, logi-tf-sim-0.42.0.cdx.json) and is attached to the release of that tag: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/releases
osps_br_07_02_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md, Secrets: where each credential lives, who can access it, and when it is rotated.
osps_do_03_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#verifying-a-release: import the key, check the fingerprint, gpg --verify each asset; pacman verifies the Arch repository.
osps_do_03_02_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#verifying-a-release: the release identity is the project's GnuPG key, fingerprint published in the README and shipped with each release; a change of key is announced there.
osps_do_05_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md: a release stops receiving security updates the moment a newer release is published.
osps_gv_04_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md, Becoming a co-maintainer: contribution history reviewed and two-factor authentication confirmed before any write or administrative access; least privilege; withdrawal after a year of inactivity.
osps_qa_02_02_justification: From 0.42.0 the release pipeline attaches a CycloneDX SBOM per Rust binary (.github/workflows/publish-release.yml, job sbom), generated from the locked dependency graph at the tag; the kernel module has no third-party components. The generation step runs in CI on every push.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md and the wiki's Building and Contributing page, Running tests: what runs, how to invoke it, and that CI runs all of it on every push and pull request.
osps_qa_06_03_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md: a change that adds functionality carries the tests for it; a bug fix carries a test that would have caught the bug.
osps_qa_07_01_justification: One maintainer; no second human approves changes to master. Recorded in GOVERNANCE.md as the first thing a co-maintainer changes.
osps_sa_03_02_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, Attack surface and threat model, and the paragraph naming the critical code paths.
osps_vm_04_02_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/security/openvex.json: OpenVEX statements for every dependency advisory that does not affect the project, with the reason.
osps_vm_05_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, Remediation thresholds: 14 days for high or critical, before the next release for the rest and for license problems.
osps_vm_05_02_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md: no release is cut with an unrecorded advisory outstanding; non-affecting advisories are recorded in the VEX document first.
osps_vm_05_03_justification: cargo audit runs on every push and pull request and fails on any advisory not recorded as non-affecting; Dependabot proposes updates weekly; the policy is docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md.
osps_vm_06_01_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, Static analysis findings: clippy findings block the change; CodeQL alerts are triaged within 14 days and fixed before the next release or dismissed with a written reason.
osps_vm_06_02_justification: clippy with warnings as errors fails CI on every change; CodeQL runs on every push and pull request and its alerts gate the release per the policy above.
